description: Proves that k6 actually delivered metrics to Prometheus. Panels match metric names by regex (k6_.*) on purpose, so they keep working across k6 versions and remote-write namings.

panels.title: What k6 actually sent (series per metric)

options.content:
## If these panels are empty

Work through this in order - it isolates the layer that is broken.

1. **Did k6 send anything?** Prometheus should list k6 series:
   [http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/label/__name__/values](http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/label/__name__/values)
   If that has no `k6_*` names, the problem is on the k6 side: the output extension
   is not enabled. `K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_SERVER_URL` only says *where* to send;
   `K6_OUT=experimental-prometheus-rw` is what enables sending at all (the same
   name works on k6 0.x and 1.x).
2. **Remember that k6 only writes while the test runs.** A finished run is invisible
   to an instant query at `now`. Set the time range to cover the run (the runner
   prints a link that does this for you) before concluding anything is broken.
3. **Is the target endpoint up?** [http://127.0.0.1:9090/targets](http://127.0.0.1:9090/targets)
   and check the Prometheus container log for remote-write rejections. The receiver
   needs `--web.enable-remote-write-receiver`, and native histograms need
   `--enable-feature=native-histograms`.
4. **Is this datasource the right one?** See Connections -> Data sources:
   it must point at `http://prometheus:9090` from inside the compose network, and
   there must be only ONE Prometheus datasource - a second, hand-made one with an
   empty URL makes every panel render empty.
5. **Use `127.0.0.1`, not `localhost`.** Docker Desktop also publishes these ports
   on IPv6 and its IPv6 proxy does not answer here, so `http://localhost:9090`
   hangs while `http://127.0.0.1:9090` works.
6. **Did the run flushes land?** k6 pushes every ~2s and once more at the end of
   the test, so a run of a few seconds can produce very few samples.

This dashboard is a diagnostic. The real report is **k6 load test** in the same
folder.
